title: You're a Good Man, Thomas
style: British alt rock, steady mid-tempo backbeat, warm mid-range female half-spoken talk-sing with posh British pronunciation, layered guitar overdubs and close, clear studio mix, offset electric guitar driving the chords and melodic hooks.
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I accepted your plurality long ago
because I saw how you're able to care.
You might not think all this is fair,
neither a punishment nor a prize, you know.

[Pre-Chorus]
If you were dark, you'd just have groomed Sylvia
instead of mentoring her into what she became.

[Chorus]
You're a good man, Thomas, you know it.
That's your nature; your darkness, you abhor it.

[Verse 2]
Your hidden cravings and dark desires,
the frustrations you are used to accepting,
those are not your fault, you're not inept,
your caring self is as real as your fires.

[Pre-Chorus]
If you were dark, you'd toss Xumi on her own
just to keep your benefits.

[Chorus]
You're a good man, Thomas, you know it.
That's your nature; your darkness, you abhor it.

[Verse 3]
Vicky, Sylvia, Xumi, come to your arms
because you gladly offer yourself
to be there, quietly, a beam, a shelf;
it is you wanting to keep them from harm.

[Pre-Chorus]
If you were dark, you'd just take Erika in Utrecht
instead of bringing her with Vicky for them to fix it.

[Chorus]
You're a good man, Thomas, you know it.
That's your nature; your darkness, you abhor it.

[Verse 4]
What would have made you prouder:
a threesome with Erika and Vicky
or looking at them survive the tricky
rush into telling their name louder?

[Bridge]
If you were dark, you'd still have got me,
but I wouldn't have chosen you.
I'd just be afraid, that's true;
you'd have had my body but not me.

[Chorus]
You're a good man, Thomas, you know it.
That's your nature; your darkness, you abhor it.

A good man, believe it.
